name: Nat Pagle
summary: Nat Pagle is widely hailed as the most renowned angler in all of Azeroth, despite claiming he only fishes as an excuse to drink heavily. He makes his home on a secluded inlet in Dustwallow Marsh, where he trains elite anglers from both the Alliance and the Horde who manage to prove their patience.

sections.title: The Master Angler
sections.body: Though his name is synonymous with angling mastery across the known world, Nat Pagle is remarkably casual about his craft. Having cast lines for several decades, he often admits he has no great reverence for the sport itself, famously calling it little more than a convenient excuse to sit back and drink heavily. Despite this gruff nonchalance, Nat understands aquatic life and the art of angling better than anyone alive, even authoring his own guide and licensing fishing gear sought out by professionals.

sections.title: A Marshland Hermit
sections.body: Pagle makes his camp on a small spit of land along the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, far from the bustling taverns of the Eastern Kingdoms. He remains fiercely independent and uninterested in the politics of factions, welcoming Alliance travelers sent by trainers like Grimnur Stonebrand as well as Horde aspirants directed to him by Lumak in Orgrimmar. For Nat, anyone willing to scour the corners of the world for rare specimens deserves a lesson in genuine angling.

sections.title: Old Tales and Sea Monsters
sections.body: Before settling in Kalimdor, Nat spent his earlier years fishing the docks of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills, where he frequently baffled his angling partners with vivid, prophetic dreams of historical upheavals. Pagle has also ventured into far more perilous waters, including an excursion into the ruins of Zul'Gurub where he misplaced his favorite measuring tape and tackle box near the waters prowled by the monstrous hydra Gahz'ranka.

faq.answer: Nat Pagle is the most famous fisherman in Azeroth. Having angled for decades, he now lives a quiet life along the coast of Dustwallow Marsh, training veteran anglers who have outgrown ordinary trainers.

faq.q: Where can Nat Pagle be found?
faq.answer: He lives on a small spit of land known as Pagle's Pointe, located on the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh in Kalimdor, southwest of Theramore Isle.

faq.q: Why does Nat Pagle fish if he says he dislikes it?
faq.answer: Pagle has candidly confessed that he views fishing primarily as a respectable, undisturbed excuse to sit by the water and drink heavily for hours at a time.

faq.q: Will Nat Pagle train members of the Horde?
faq.answer: Yes. Nat is entirely neutral toward faction rivalries. Horde anglers who reach the upper limits of ordinary skill are sent directly to him by his friend Lumak in Orgrimmar.

faq.q: What connection does Nat Pagle have to Zul'Gurub?
faq.answer: Nat once fished within the ancient troll city of Zul'Gurub, leaving behind his tackle box and prized measuring tape near the waters harboring the great hydra Gahz'ranka.

faq.q: Where did Nat Pagle come from originally?
faq.answer: Years ago, Nat fished the southern docks of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills alongside fellow locals, long before he decided to cross the Great Sea to Kalimdor.

angles.text: Lumak, the fishing trainer in the Valley of Honor in Orgrimmar, counts Nat Pagle as a trusted friend and sends promising Horde fishermen across the sea to train with him.
Dwarven master anglers such as Grimnur Stonebrand in Ironforge hold Nat in high esteem, sending experienced Alliance fishermen down to Dustwallow Marsh to learn the craft's final secrets.
